name: What is the best order of work for ADU bathroom construction?

mainEntity.name: In what sequence should the bathroom be built so the project stays efficient and avoids rework?
mainEntity.text: In what sequence should the bathroom be built so the project stays efficient and avoids rework?

acceptedAnswer.text: The best order for ADU bathroom construction usually starts with framing, followed by rough plumbing and rough electrical. After those are inspected, waterproofing goes in, then tile or wall finishes, then the fixtures, trim, and final inspection. This sequence matters because each stage depends on the previous one being complete and correct. If waterproofing starts before rough-in is approved, or if fixtures are changed after tile is set, the project can become expensive very quickly. Homeowners should also choose fixture sizes and finishes early enough that the rough openings, drain locations, and electrical placement match the final design. In a small ADU bathroom, the order of work is especially important because there is little room to absorb mistakes. A good contractor should be able to explain the sequence clearly and tell you what has to be approved before the next phase begins. That clarity is one of the best signs that the project is well managed.
acceptedAnswer.description: The typical order is framing, rough plumbing, rough electrical, inspections, waterproofing, tile or wall finishes, fixture installation, trim, and final inspection. Deviating from that sequence can create leaks, failed inspections, or expensive rework. Bathroom materials should be selected early so framing and rough-in match the final layout.
